decision_brief.authoring_note: Written fresh for the iteration-03 rebuild of the 2026-09-29 snapshot. Implements the round-2 instruction set: the Fed proxy value now sits under the tenor-correct key (implied_monthly_average_rate), the overbroad correction notes are replaced by exact-location statements, and the renderer consumption update is prepared as the separate frontend change required by the repository's data/frontend separation contract. No market value changed; every number derives from the captures bound in the iteration-01 evidence directory.
decision_brief.headline: Both central banks are on hold — Fed 3.75-4.00% into Oct 27-28, BoC 2.25% into Oct 28 — and the contracts we can verify sit just above policy rather than at a dislocation: the October Fed average 2 bp above the range midpoint, CORRA futures 12.5 bp above target. With FedWatch still dark (403), the week's actionable risk lives in the release calendar — JOLTS today, Q2 GDP and PCE Wednesday, payrolls Friday — not in either policy rate.
decision_brief.summary: This remains an abstention on position, not on view. Both boards hold, with the next decisions inside five weeks, and the only pricing that survives verification is contract-level: ZQV26, the October 30-day Fed funds contract, closed 96.105 on Sep 28, implying a 3.895% October monthly (30-day) average EFFR — 2 bp above the 3.875% midpoint of the 3.75-4.00% target range — while CRAU26's quote side (97.62/97.625) implies roughly 2.375% quarterly average CORRA, 12.5 bp above the 2.25% target across both the Oct 28 and Dec 9 decisions. Neither is a meeting probability; FedWatch returned HTTP 403 again, so no single-meeting distribution exists anywhere in this snapshot and none is estimated. Monday's strip was risk-draining (SPY -0.74%, TLT -0.88%, XLF -1.19%, GLD -3.94%) — recorded without a causal claim. The consumer is where the asymmetry sits: Michigan's final 48.1 beat the 47.6 consensus yet was the lowest reading in four months, and Canada's July retail sales contracted 0.7% headline / 1.1% volume. The rates are patient; the data will not be.
